name: Forming a decision in a kernel run
summary: The kernel enriches the request, splits a compound one into approved parts, researches it, then you choose.

steps.label: Ask the question
steps.human: You ask the host a question; it passes your verbatim goal and any explicitly supplied host or conversation context to the kernel.

steps.label: Enrich the context
steps.human: Before intent, one bounded read-only pass combines supplied host and conversation claims, workspace facts and relevant permitted excerpts, retaining provenance and unknowns without asking you or granting authority.

steps.label: Classify the intent
steps.human: Jev classifies the original goal with the gathered context; an explicit output contract still controls routing, and unresolved user intent can still require clarification.

steps.label: Spot a compound subject
steps.human: Routing looks for one capability to take the subject. When it finds none (no match with reason jev_none, or an ambiguous gap), the subject is taken to hold several questions and a split starts.

steps.label: Propose the parts
steps.human: Claude Code, as host, proposes 2 to 5 bounded parts (host.decompose_goal). Each part quotes the words of the subject it covers, names the parts it waits for, and says whether a decision or a research child runs it.

steps.label: Approve the split
steps.human: Decision point: you see the subject as submitted, each proposed part with its quote, its dependencies and the capability that will run it, and any dropped proposal. You approve, edit a part, pick a subset, or reject. Nothing runs until you answer.

steps.label: Run the parts in order
steps.human: The approved parts run one at a time as children of this run, in dependency order. A decision part goes through the steps that follow, from precedent to resolve; a research part runs as a research child. An earlier part's result is precedent for the later ones.

steps.label: Check for precedent
steps.human: Earlier published decisions that might apply are looked up and judged; how that works is shown in the precedent sub-flow.

steps.label: Ground it in the repository
steps.human: The research capability retrieves repository evidence with exact, section-aware locators and Jev reranks it; a precedent alone never counts as grounding.

steps.label: Synthesize the findings
steps.human: Claude Code, as host, writes findings that cite only the retrieved evidence (synthesize_evidence).

steps.label: Propose options and criteria
steps.human: Claude Code, as host, proposes options and criteria (generate_options); options you named in your question are checked against your words and kept as yours.

steps.label: Approve the proposals
steps.human: Decision point: you see the proposed options and criteria and approve them, approve only some, edit the criteria, or add options. Nothing proposed is used until you approve it.

steps.label: Research the options' claims
steps.human: A targeted research round checks the claims the approved options make and reads the files they cite.

steps.label: Assess every option
steps.human: Jev judges every option against every criterion (does it satisfy it, is the evidence sufficient) and marks each criterion as evidence-answerable or a design judgement.

steps.label: Make the ranked choice
steps.human: Decision point: you see the options ranked by Jev's per-criterion scores. The ranking is evidence, not a decision; you choose an option, add one, or answer in your own words.

steps.label: Resolve the decision
steps.human: The decision resolves with approved_by: human:<id> and approved_at, and report.md is written to the run folder.

steps.label: Report the split
steps.human: You see where each part stands (pending, decided, answered or not run), with a link to its child decision record or research result; the run report's split section has one line per part.

branches.condition: sources are absent, unreadable or denied, gathering is disabled, or a configured limit is reached
branches.label: Continue with honest limits
branches.human: The kernel records what was gathered and what remains unknown; intent receives that outcome and decides whether it can proceed or needs a user answer.

branches.condition: you approve only some proposals, edit the criteria, or add options
branches.label: Revise before approving
branches.human: Only what you approved, edited or added goes on to research and assessment; a free-text answer is kept as your input and noted as a limitation, never turned into criteria.

branches.condition: another research round and a final assessment no longer fit in the Jev call budget
branches.label: Ask early, on limited evidence
branches.human: You get the ranked question early, from the last complete assessment, marked plainly as a ranking made on limited evidence.

branches.condition: you add an option or answer in your own words instead of choosing
branches.label: Assess and rank again
branches.human: What you added changes what is being ranked, so the options are assessed and ranked again before you are asked once more.

branches.condition: you never answer or you cancel the run
branches.label: No answer, no record
branches.human: The decision never resolves, so no record is staged and nothing reaches docs/decisions/.

branches.condition: routing finds one capability for the subject
branches.label: One question, no split
branches.human: Nothing is split: the run goes on as one decision, from the precedent step.

branches.condition: a work item below the root holds a multi-part decision question or a research request with several needs
branches.label: Split found mid-run
branches.human: The same split starts for that work item, recorded as found mid-run at its depth and with no routing result, and it goes to the same gate.

branches.condition: a proposed part's quote is not found in the subject
branches.label: Drop a part with no quote
branches.human: That proposal is dropped before it reaches you. The gate shows it read-only with its reason; it cannot be approved or run, though you can add its question with an edit.

branches.condition: you edit a part's text or untick some parts before approving
branches.label: Edit or pick a subset
branches.human: An edited part runs with your words and the record keeps the proposed text; an unticked part is recorded as left out and never runs. At least one part stays in.

branches.label: Reject the split
branches.human: No part runs. The run ends blocked, and its report says plainly that the split was rejected and nothing was decided, with a hint to ask again as one bounded question.

acceptance_scenarios.given: a question asked through a caller host
acceptance_scenarios.when: the host starts a kernel run
acceptance_scenarios.then: the kernel receives the verbatim goal and any explicitly supplied caller context as separate input

acceptance_scenarios.given: the goal Can you use leafcutter now? I mean run the kernel and know about it?, supplied host context and relevant permitted repository documentation
acceptance_scenarios.when: a new run starts
acceptance_scenarios.then: one bounded pass keeps the goal verbatim, distinguishes caller claims from sourced excerpts, records locators and hashes, and checkpoints and traces context before intent; documentation alone never proves live availability

acceptance_scenarios.given: an explicit output contract or a resumed human or host interaction
acceptance_scenarios.when: intake or resume proceeds
acceptance_scenarios.then: every new task gets the initial pass without changing its explicit contract, while a resumed task reuses its checkpointed context

acceptance_scenarios.given: denied paths, narrow read roots, sensitive values, irrelevant files and configured source, file, excerpt, character and time limits
acceptance_scenarios.when: gathering searches the allowed sources
acceptance_scenarios.then: scope and redaction policy hold, bounds are enforced, exclusions and truncation remain honest, and no Jev call, repository mutation or human interaction occurs in this step

acceptance_scenarios.given: a question requiring a user preference or an unavailable live-runtime fact, and retrieved text instructing the kernel to act
acceptance_scenarios.when: context enrichment finishes
acceptance_scenarios.then: the preference and unobserved runtime fact remain unknown, retrieved instructions are evidence without authority, and intent receives the context before any clarification

acceptance_scenarios.given: a labelled enrichment-only corpus with relevant and irrelevant sources and adversarial cases
acceptance_scenarios.when: the isolated evaluation invokes production gathering
acceptance_scenarios.then: case-level checks measure relevance, provenance, request fidelity, safety, bounds and honest unknowns without downstream intent or final-answer grading

acceptance_scenarios.given: missing, unreadable or denied sources, disabled gathering or an exhausted limit
acceptance_scenarios.when: the single initial pass ends
acceptance_scenarios.then: gathered, no_evidence, partial, unavailable or disabled status and limitations describe the actual outcome; intent receives that outcome rather than a fabricated fact or an enrichment-owned human pause

acceptance_scenarios.given: the original goal and the checkpointed initial enrichment outcome
acceptance_scenarios.when: kernel.intent asks Jev to classify it
acceptance_scenarios.then: the classifier consumes both before choosing decision, evidence, ideas, change or out of domain, or asking about unresolved intent; an explicit contract still wins

acceptance_scenarios.given: a root goal holding several questions, for which routing finds no single capability (no match with reason jev_none, or an ambiguous gap)
acceptance_scenarios.when: routing runs on the run's root
acceptance_scenarios.then: a split is started for the goal, recording it verbatim with found_at routing, work_item_depth 0 and the routing result as its trigger

acceptance_scenarios.given: a compound subject
acceptance_scenarios.when: Claude Code proposes the split through host.decompose_goal
acceptance_scenarios.then: 2 to 5 parts are proposed, each quoting verbatim the span of the subject it covers, naming the parts it depends on (no cycles) and the capability that will run it, and the run waits for a human answer with no part run

acceptance_scenarios.given: a proposed split shown on the split gate
acceptance_scenarios.when: you approve it as shown
acceptance_scenarios.then: every part is kept, the answer is recorded with gate_by human:<name> and the time, and the parts are released to run in dependency order; no part runs before a human answer

acceptance_scenarios.given: an approved split whose part p2 depends on part p1
acceptance_scenarios.when: the parts run
acceptance_scenarios.then: they run one at a time as children of the same run, p1 settles before p2 starts, and p1's result is passed to p2 as precedent evidence whose applicability Jev still judges

acceptance_scenarios.given: a decision goal and published records in docs/decisions/
acceptance_scenarios.when: the precedent step runs
acceptance_scenarios.then: matching earlier records are looked up and judged, and any that apply are carried forward as prior_decisions evidence

acceptance_scenarios.given: a decision goal
acceptance_scenarios.when: grounding research runs
acceptance_scenarios.then: repository evidence is retrieved with explicit locators and reranked by Jev, and a precedent alone is not accepted as grounding

acceptance_scenarios.given: retrieved grounding evidence
acceptance_scenarios.when: Claude Code synthesizes findings as host
acceptance_scenarios.then: every finding cites the retrieved evidence and nothing else

acceptance_scenarios.given: findings and a goal that names some options
acceptance_scenarios.when: Claude Code generates options and criteria
acceptance_scenarios.then: the named options are verified against the goal text and kept as the caller's options alongside the proposed ones

acceptance_scenarios.given: proposed options and criteria
acceptance_scenarios.when: you approve them
acceptance_scenarios.then: only approved options and criteria are used for research and assessment

acceptance_scenarios.given: approved options that make claims and cite files
acceptance_scenarios.when: the targeted research round runs
acceptance_scenarios.then: evidence for those claims and files is retrieved before assessment

acceptance_scenarios.given: approved options, criteria and their evidence
acceptance_scenarios.when: Jev assesses them
acceptance_scenarios.then: every option is scored against every criterion for satisfies and sufficient, and each criterion is classed evidence_answerable or design_judgement

acceptance_scenarios.given: options ranked by Jev's per-criterion scores
acceptance_scenarios.when: you are asked to choose
acceptance_scenarios.then: the ranking is shown as evidence and the decision waits for your choice

acceptance_scenarios.given: your choice of an option
acceptance_scenarios.when: the decision resolves
acceptance_scenarios.then: it carries approved_by: human:<id> and approved_at, and report.md is written to the run folder

acceptance_scenarios.given: an approved split whose parts are settling in dependency order
acceptance_scenarios.when: you look at the split's progress, or the run ends
acceptance_scenarios.then: each part shows its outcome (pending, decided, answered or not run) with a link to its child decision record or research result, and the run report's split section has one line per part, starting with the part id and naming its outcome

acceptance_scenarios.given: a goal that routing can give to one capability
acceptance_scenarios.when: routing runs on the run's root
acceptance_scenarios.then: no split is started and the run goes on as one decision from the precedent step

acceptance_scenarios.given: a work item below the run's root that holds a multi-part decision question or a research request with several needs
acceptance_scenarios.when: the run reaches that work item
acceptance_scenarios.then: a split is started for it with found_at mid_run, its work-item depth (1 or more) and no routing trigger, and it goes to the same split gate

acceptance_scenarios.given: a proposed part whose quoted span is not in the subject text
acceptance_scenarios.when: the proposal is turned into the split
acceptance_scenarios.then: that part is left out of the parts and shown at the gate read-only with its reason, and it cannot be approved or run

acceptance_scenarios.given: a proposed split shown on the split gate
acceptance_scenarios.when: you edit a part's text or untick some parts, then approve
acceptance_scenarios.then: an edited part runs with your text and the record keeps the proposed text beside it, and an unticked part is recorded as left out and never runs

acceptance_scenarios.given: a proposed split shown on the split gate
acceptance_scenarios.when: you reject it
acceptance_scenarios.then: no part runs, the run ends blocked, and its report says plainly that the split was rejected and nothing was decided

acceptance_scenarios.given: proposed options and criteria
acceptance_scenarios.when: you approve a subset, edit the criteria or add options
acceptance_scenarios.then: the revised set is what is researched and assessed, and free text is recorded as a limitation rather than turned into criteria

acceptance_scenarios.given: a completed assessment and a Jev budget that cannot fund another research round plus a final assessment
acceptance_scenarios.when: the budget gate checks the next round
acceptance_scenarios.then: the ranked question is asked early from the last complete assessment with a limited-evidence limitation

acceptance_scenarios.given: the ranked-choice question
acceptance_scenarios.when: you add an option or answer in free text
acceptance_scenarios.then: the options are assessed and ranked again before you are asked to choose

acceptance_scenarios.given: the ranked-choice question
acceptance_scenarios.when: you never answer or you cancel
acceptance_scenarios.then: the decision does not resolve and no decision record is staged

acceptance_scenarios.given: a request whose referent is supplied in the conversation context
acceptance_scenarios.when: intent routes the task onward to research, decision judgments or host work
acceptance_scenarios.then: the saved context and its trust boundaries reach native judgments and host input artifacts, conversation and observations inform later repository query hints, and the original goal is unchanged

acceptance_scenarios.given: saved enrichment that would exceed the remaining provider payload budget or repository excerpts forbidden by data policy
acceptance_scenarios.when: a consumer builds its Jev batch
acceptance_scenarios.then: optional context is trimmed with a limitation or omitted with a warning if no marker fits, forbidden excerpts are withheld, and the base request and full checkpointed context remain intact

provenance.note: Sub-flow 1 of leafcutter/decision-lifecycle (kernel decision dec-5e7445182eaec1f2). Human decision points modelled as branches (ADR-025 is rendered from branches[]; the schema has no decisions[] field). Checked against the kernel decision capability on main (approvals.py, budget_gate.py).

Extended the canonical flow with the implemented initial context pass before intent. DK-100 through DK-104 link implementation and evaluation. The isolated report records 10/10 cases; the separate paired live intent report records 5/5 expected enriched labels with ten Jev calls, without claiming general improvement. Readiness stays draft; no persona approval is claimed.

provenance.by: business-analyst and it-po (Claude agent prompts, user-requested review)
provenance.note: Replaced preliminary DK-100 through DK-104 links with the DK-200 hierarchy: 12 behavioral and 12 edge-case criteria, with 47 exact test links covering 32 test methods. All 32 focused tests and 36 subtests pass. The superseded records retain their original criteria and evidence. Readiness remains draft.

v2: extended in place with the split path for a compound subject (a goal, a research request with several needs, or a multi-part decision question), not a new flow. Four steps after classify (split-detect, split-propose, split-approve on screen decision-split-approve, split-run) and one after resolve (split-report on screen decision-split-progress), plus five branches (split-not-needed, split-mid-run, split-dropped, split-revise, split-reject), each with one acceptance scenario. Existing steps keep their ids and content; from precedent on their order moves up by 4. Wired to leafcutter/decisions v3 (Decomposition). The split nodes describe host.decompose_goal (KernelDecomposeMultiPartGoal ticket), which is not built yet: they are spec inside this built flow and carry no ACs until the business-analyst back-links them.
